newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady as market eyes Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady as market eyes Taiwan.

text.p: The lull in the gasoline market continued on Tuesday as traders sought firmer direction from Taiwan, traders said.

Some traders expected offers into Taiwan's buy tender for July 24-August 15 delivery of 250,000-barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate to be higher than the last July 16-30 purchase at $24.76 per barrel c+f.
"Prices in Singapore have firmed since then," said a trader.
Market rumours of a U.S. major offering 100,000 barrels lifting July from Jurong on par to Singapore spot quotes, fob, was denied.
Another rumour of a 80,000-barrel cargo sold by another U.S. major at a 10 cent discount could not be confirmed by market close.
But some traders thought the level was too high.
"Buyers were only at $1.00 to 50 cents in discount... it is hard to believe anyone would improve to 10 cents," said a trader.
Traders assessed the discount more at 50-40 cents per barrel.
Naphtha fell amid ample supplies and weak demand.
July swaps fell marginally to $21.10/$21.20 per barrel from Monday's $21.10/$21.30.
India is to export around five to six naphtha cargoes in July, and has offered the first two cargoes from the west coast in two tenders, both closing June 19.

The first tender issued by state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) offered 25,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting July 2-4 from Bombay and the second 30,000 tonnes of HAN lifting June 30-July 2 from Cochin, industry sources said.
